20,00,000/- may kindly be awarded to him.

Contents of paras 8 to 11 have specifically been contested by denying the fact that the accident in question had taken place.

21. The proceedings under the M.V. Act are of summary in nature, where liability of tort-feasor is to be fixed, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.
rt Although, proceedings under the M.V. Act are summary in nature, but, it does not mean that whatsoever pleaded by the petitioner, in the petition, is to be considered and taken as gospel truth.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable, but some evidence should be there to probabilize the case of the petitioner.
22. In this case, issues were framed on 18.11.2011.
Thereafter, five effective opportunities were given by the learned Tribunal to the petitioner to lead his evidence.
Firstly, the case was fixed for recording the evidence of petitioner's witnesses on 19.9.2011.
Thereafter, the case was fixed for 25.11.2011, 22.2.2012, 28.4.2012 and 30.5.2012.
Thereafter, vide order dated 30.7.2012, the learned Tribunal closed the evidence of the petitioner.
The order dated 30.7.2012 is reproduced as .

under:
"No Pw present.
Though vide order dated 7.7.2012 the petitioner was directed to bring all sort of evidence of his own for today.
He was made aware of the fact that if no evidence would be produced by him, it would be closed by the court order.
The case pertains to the year of 2006.
The perusal of the file shows that the case was enlisted for the evidence of the petitioner on 01.07.2011, 19.09.2011, 25.11.2011 and 22.02.2012.
On all these rt dates no Pws were present.
PWs were not summoned as steps were not taken.
Still opportunities were granted for 26.4.2012, 30.5.2012 and 30.07.2012.
I am of the view that no further opportunity can be granted to the petitioner for leading further evidence.
As such, his evidence is closed by court order.
Put up for RWS for 27.08.2012.
Let Rws be summoned on taking steps for the said date."

23. The petitioner himself has appeared in the witness box as PW-1 and deposed that on 15.6.2006,
he alongwith his family members had gone to Koti, Badon.

24. According to him, due to accident, his efficiency has been rt decreased, as he had qualified ACC examination, in the year 2005.

Due to the accident, he had come in the category of 'Low Medical Category', resulting into the fact that he could not get any promotion.
He has further deposed that an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- has been spent, on his treatment.
In his cross-examination, this witness has admitted that he has not annexed any document that he was on leave, at the relevant time.
As per him, at the of relevant time, he was posted at Moonoom Cantt., Pathankot.
27. rt PW-2 Manju Sharma, is younger sister of the petitioner.
She has supported the case of her brother, regarding the manner, in which the accident in question had taken place.
She has deposed that after the accident, she brought her brother to Shimla.
28. On the other hand, respondents had examined Chet Singh Thakur, Junior Assistant in the SDM Office, Shimla.
He has deposed that Shyam Singh was the owner of vehicle No. HP-51B-0385.

He has proved the copy of Registration Certificate, Ext. RW1/A.

31 So far as, the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that he has not been given reasonable opportunities, to lead evidence, is concerned, the said submission holds no water, as the learned Tribunal has afforded reasonable opportunities to the petitioner, but, despite those opportunities, having been afforded to him, he could not adduce evidence.

32. The respondents have placed on record certified copy of the judgment, dated 8.5.2009, passed in Criminal case No. 17/2 of 2007, titled as, 'State of H.P. versus Rajender Singh', which is Ext.
RW2/A.

From the perusal of this document, one thing is crystal clear that .
the accident in question had taken place with the offending vehicle, upon which, the FIR in question has been registered against respondent No. 2.

The of Registration of the FIR in question,
prima-facie, proves that the accident in question had taken place, due to rt rash and negligent driving of respondent No. 2.
33.

Judging the document, Ext. RW2/A, on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities, there is no legal hesitation, for this Court, to hold that the offending vehicle was being driven, by respondent No.2, in a rash and negligent manner.
However, from this document, this fact has not been probabilised that the petitioner had sustained any injury or remained admit in the hospital.

34. Now, coming to the effect of the evidence, so adduced, by the parties, from the stand as taken by the respondents' witnesses, Ext. RW2/A is the copy of judgment, dated 8.5.2009, in criminal Case No. 17/2 of 2007, titled as, 'State of H.P. versus Rajender Singh'.

accident in question had taken place, as registration of the FIR, upon which, the trial has been commenced, against respondent No. 2, prima-facie, proves that the of accident in question had taken place.

35. Judging this document on the touchstone of the rt preponderance of probabilities, this can be said that the accident in question had taken place with the offending vehicle, being driven by respondent No. 2, in a rash and negligent manner.
